questions.label: The table
questions.prompt: It's your last meal. Who's at the table?

options.label: Just you, with the radio on low
Three people, chosen carefully, no agenda
Anyone who can make it — kids, cousins, the loud ones
The people who can't be there, named and set for
Your grandmother's kitchen — the same one
A quiet sushi counter with a chef who says little
A long table in a loud, family-run trattoria
A blanket in a park at the hour the light goes soft
Just after sunrise, when the kitchen is still cool
Midday, the room at its loudest
Early evening, with candles lit one by one
Past midnight, at a counter that never closes

questions.label: One detail
questions.prompt: There's one detail you'd insist on. Pick it.

options.label: The salt is passed hand to hand, never left on the table
Bread that was baked the same morning
The music is a person playing, not a speaker
One full minute of silence before anyone eats
Tea in a chipped cup you've had since childhood
A bottle someone brought, opened but not talked up
Cold water, refilled without asking
Coffee, dark, in a cup you hold the whole meal

questions.label: The leftover
questions.prompt: What you do with the leftovers says a lot. You...

options.label: Box them up for whoever left last
Leave them — this was meant to be finished tonight
Hand them to a stranger on the way home
Write down the recipe so it can be made again
Breaking it in half and giving one piece away
Holding it in your mouth longer than you need to
Asking someone to photograph the plate before you finish
Leaving it on the plate, on purpose, so it isn't gone

archetypes.label: Grandmother's Kitchen
archetypes.tagline: A warm, plain table that tastes like every meal you've ever been loved at.
archetypes.blindSpot: Memory can become a museum when a new kitchen would have been the point.

archetypes.label: Quiet Sushi Counter
archetypes.tagline: A few perfect pieces, eaten slowly, with no one asking how it was.
archetypes.blindSpot: Restraint can read as coldness when the table needed a little noise.

archetypes.label: Loud Trattoria
archetypes.tagline: A long table, second helpings, and a conversation that runs past the candles.
archetypes.blindSpot: Generosity can spill over into spectacle when a quiet night would have done.

archetypes.label: Picnic Blanket
archetypes.tagline: A blanket, a paper bag, and an hour the light goes soft in.
archetypes.blindSpot: Romance can skip the part where someone still has to pack the bag.

archetypes.label: Midnight Diner
archetypes.tagline: A counter that never closes, a stranger who nods, and the comfort of last call.
archetypes.blindSpot: Solitude can harden into lonerdom when a table of three would have been warmer.
